title: connection-kind
description: A plugin-shipped connection contract: the settings a connection of this kind carries.

$schema.description: The kind of this document: its published schema URL, or the alias @wilanis/connection-kind.schema.json.

description.description: What this kind of connection reaches, in one or two sentences.

label.description: A short human name for this document, shown wherever a reader sees it instead of its path. Absent: the file name stands in.

storage.description: true: a connection of this kind reaches a storage engine, so an @storage store may name it. The plugin that grants the kind registers the engine behind it.

capabilities.description: What the storage engine behind a connection of this kind can do: the three facts a rule or the migration planner reads (RFC 0022). Required where `storage` is true, with no default, since an engine's limits are a fact its kind document states. Written by the plugin that grants the kind, never by a tree's author. Not the word a profile's `permits` speaks: that is what an environment allows a tree to do, and this is what an engine can do.

transactionalDdl.description: true: a migration plan applies in one transaction on this engine, so a step that fails leaves the database as it was (RFC 0017). false: the plan applies step by step, the record kept after each.

unique.description: The field classes a collection's `unique` may name over a connection of this kind (RFC 0003): string, number, boolean, shape, list, unknown -- every shape is one class and every list another. [] when the engine constrains nothing.

refs.description: true: the engine enforces a collection's `refs` (RFC 0003): a write naming a record that does not exist, and a remove of a record another still names, are refused by the store.

leases.description: true: a connection of this kind can keep a lease -- a named hold one process of several takes for a while, and the record of what was last done under it. The plugin that grants the kind registers a lease keeper for it; the scheduler's `run` step names such a connection as its `lease` (X254). Absent: a connection of this kind keeps no lease (an HTTP upstream, a directory).

delivery.description: How many times a connection of this kind may hand one message to a trigger that receives from it. at-least-once: a message the process did not acknowledge is delivered again, so what it fires may run twice. at-most-once: a message is handed once and never again, so what it fires may not run at all. The plugin that grants the kind registers the broker behind it. Absent: a connection of this kind delivers nothing (an HTTP upstream, a directory).

endpoint.description: Which of this kind's settings holds the address a connection of this kind reaches: a dotted path into `settings` (`baseUrl`, `broker.url`) naming a string setting (C020). Declared: a deployment lists the connection among what the environment must provide. Absent: a connection of this kind reaches nothing outside the tree, or reaches something no deployment provisions.

if.description: `storage` is what makes a kind an engine's, so it is what asks for the facts about that engine.

storage.description: Selects the rules of a kind whose connections reach a storage engine.

then.description: A storage kind says what its engine can do: there is no default for an engine's limits.
